name: Analogy of Scripture

objectives.text: Identify the Bible as one book from God that tells one true story from beginning to end
Name the Bible itself as the best helper for understanding other parts of the Bible
Explain that the parts of the Bible always agree with each other because God, who gave it, always tells the truth
Match a short Bible verse with another verse that teaches the same truth
State the rule that Scripture interprets Scripture in your own words and give an example of one passage explaining another
Locate related passages using the cross-reference notes in a study Bible
Explain why Reformed interpreters use clearer passages to help understand passages that are harder to understand
Compare two passages on the same subject and write a summary that includes what each contributes
Describe how Jesus answered a misused Scripture by setting it beside another Scripture during his temptation
Gather passages with a concordance on a key word and explain why a shared word does not always carry the same meaning in every passage
Compare parallel Gospel accounts of the same event and explain how the details fit together into a fuller picture
Analyze the apparent contradiction between Paul and James on justification by comparing how each uses the words faith, works, and justify
Explain how the Reformed tradition grounds the analogy of Scripture in the single divine authorship of the whole Bible
Evaluate an interpretation that builds a teaching on one isolated verse against the wider testimony of Scripture
Differentiate the analogy of Scripture from the analogy of faith and explain how creeds summarize the rule of faith drawn from Scripture
Construct a doctrinal summary on a topic such as the Trinity by gathering, comparing, and ordering passages from across the Bible
Evaluate how a New Testament author interprets an Old Testament passage by comparing the original text with its apostolic use
Explain why the Reformed tradition treats Scripture as the supreme judge over councils, traditions, and private interpretations
Evaluate a common claim that the Bible contradicts itself and defend its internal consistency using the principles of the analogy of Scripture
Produce a written study that reconciles a difficult set of parallel passages such as the accounts of David's census in Samuel and Chronicles

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (one story, Bible as its own interpreter, noncontradiction, Scripture interprets Scripture, clear interprets unclear, comparing passages, cross-references, Paul and James, apostolic use of the OT, internal consistency, systematic summary, parallel passages). Dropped typology and 'unity of the Bible' as better suited to Progressive Revelation, and 'interpret obscure passages in light of systematic theology' as vague. Added Jesus's use of Scripture in the temptation, concordance use with word-meaning caution, parallel Gospel harmonization, the doctrine's basis in divine authorship, evaluating isolated proof-texting, analogy of Scripture versus analogy of faith, and Scripture as supreme judge (WCF 1.10). Anchored references to specific verses and to WCF 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 1.9, 1.10, 11.2 and WSC Q6.
